synopsis: Epiroc (Mernok) fourth-generation collision avoidance and Titan serve mining fleets with Level 9 intervention; Titan claims full Levels 7, 8 and 9 capability using EMESRT PR-5A as a guideline [f1078, f6575]. Epiroc also describes on-site evaluation and traffic management without immediately enforcing Level 9, presented as an off-road analogue to shadow testing and an example of staged release [f587, f11754]. This staged approach contrasts with South African practice pushing Level 9 mandates [f6575]. Mernok and Epiroc reported more than ten years of development behind their fourth-generation system in May 2024 [f823, f1080]. Titan fuses several technologies, but the corpus found no independent performance test for the surveyed off-road automatic braking systems, including Epiroc's; it also groups those offerings as reverse-only, low-speed or tag-dependent without identifying Epiroc's specific restriction [f678, f1242, f1239].
